full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel, j: At the instance of the present accused-petitioner, this Rule was issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of the Sessions Case No.236 of 2017, arising out of CR Case No. 813 of 2016 (Nawab) under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chapainawabganj or Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chapainawabganj should not be quashed. 

 2. The relevant facts for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the accused-petitioner is the proprietor of M/s Zoha International. He obtained loan from the AB Bank Limited, Chapainawabganj Branch, but did not repay the loan amount. Therefore, the outstanding amount stood at Taka 2,67,98,821.90 (two crore sixty seven lac ninety eight thousand eight hundred twenty one taka ninety paisa). The bank repeatedly asked the accused-petitioner to repay the outstanding amount. However, at last he paid a cheque being No.5509769 dated 25-9-2016 of National Bank Limited of Current Account No.0005333017446. The AB Bank Limited, Chapainawabganj Branch submitted the alleged cheque in the National Bank Ltd., Chapainawabganj Branch for encashment, but it was dishonoured for insufficient fund. Thereafter, the AB Bank Limited, Chapai-nawabganj Branch sent a legal notice to the accused-petitioner on 29-9-2016 demanding the alleged amount of money. But he did not repay the said amount of money. Hence, the case. 

 3. Thereafter, on 8-11-2016 one Md Shariful Islam, Senior Officer, AB Bank Limited, Chapainawabganj branch being constituted attorney of AB Bank Limited, Chapainawabganj branch, Chapainawabganj as complainant filed a complaint case being CR Case No.813 of 2016 to the learned Cognizance Court of Senior Judicial Magistrate, `Ka' area, Chapainawabganj against the accused-petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. After hearing the complainant the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, Cognizance Court, 'Ka' Area, Chapainawabganj was pleased to take cognizance of the instant CR Case No.813 of 2016 against the accused-petitioner under section 183 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 (in short, the Act) and issued summon upon him. Thereafter, on 11-12-2016 he voluntarily surrendered before the cognizance Court of Senior Judicial Magistrate, `Ka' Area, Chapainawabganj with a prayer for bail and after hearing the application for bail, the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate granted bail to the accused-petitioner. 

 4. Subsequently, the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, Cognizance Court of 'Ka' Area, Chapainawabganj vide order dated 18-1-2017 transferred the case record to the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chapainawabganj, who on 29-1-2017 transferred the case record to the learned Sessions Judge, Chapainawabganj for trial. On 27-2-2017 the learned Sessions Judge, Chapainawabganj received the case record and it has been renumbered as Sessions Case No.236 of 2017. Then, he transferred the case to the Additional Sessions Judge, Chapainawabganj for trial and on 29-6-2017 the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chapainawabganj framed charge against the accused-petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 

 5. The accused-petitioner being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the instant proceeding of Sessions Case No.236 of 2017, arising out of CR Case No.813 of 2016 (Nawab) filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceeding of the said case and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

 6. Mr Sifat Mahmud, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner supports the Rule and submits that at the time of sanctioning loan the accused-petitioner gave his property by way of registered mortgage deed and also deposited the cheque in question as collateral security. But the complainant-bank filed the Artha Rin Case No.09 of 2017 against the accused-petitioner under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for realization of loan before the Artha Rin Court No.1, Chapainawabganj as well as filed the instant case under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 on the selfsame matter, which is highly malafide and not maintainable in the eye of law.
